newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Jewish group calls Swiss conference on Nazi loot.
newsitem.headline: Jewish group calls Swiss conference on Nazi loot.

text.p: The U.S.-based Jewish human rights group Simon Wiesenthal Centre said on Friday it was calling a conference of experts in Geneva to address the international hunt for gold, art and other property stolen by Nazi Germany.

"This will take place in Geneva on June 24-25 and will draw together political, academic, legal and clerical personalities from Europe, Israel, the United States and Latin America," the centre's European office said in a statement.
Switzerland has been the focal point of a push by world Jewish groups to find and restore property stolen by the Nazis from Jews and other Holocaust victims.

But the drive is expanding to other countries that were also neutral during World War Two as well as to Latin America and the central bank vaults of the former Allies, which still hold some 5.5 tonnes of gold stolen and recovered after the war.

The Wiesenthal centre said it was hoped representatives of the U.S., British and Swiss governments would attend the conference to talk about "Political Leadership's Responsibility to the Victims of Nazism".
The conference would also draw up a "global report card" of individual countries' efforts to restore looted property and examine legal avenues for making restitution claims.
